locked_content: Machine-learning systems depend on trustworthy training data. Training-data poisoning represents a security threat in which maliciously or improperly altered observations can influence the learning process.

Existing defenses may focus on individual properties such as statistical unusualness or dataset integrity. These properties can provide complementary evidence but do not necessarily capture the same forms of poisoning.

The study addresses the gap concerning integration and empirical evaluation of complementary integrity/provenance and sample-level anomaly evidence under controlled heterogeneous poisoning conditions.
PoisonShield combines trusted-reference integrity evidence, sample-level anomaly detection using Isolation Forest, and risk-based evidence fusion for training-data screening.
The study focuses on training-data poisoning in tabular cybersecurity datasets using the supplied MalMem and Android benchmark data and seven controlled poisoning mechanisms.
The contribution is a reproducible complementary-evidence framework evaluated across heterogeneous poisoning mechanisms rather than a claim of universal poisoning protection.
